result.question: How has Nvidia's data center business contributed to its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years?
result.answer:
Nvidia's data center business has been the primary engine of its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years (FY 2024, FY 2025, and FY 2026), with total revenue rising from $60.9 billion in FY 2024 to $130.5 billion in FY 2025 and then to $215.9 billion in FY 2026 [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2024-01-28] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-01-26] [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25].

**Fiscal Year 2024 (ended January 28, 2024):** Nvidia reported that demand for its data center systems and products surged in fiscal year 2024 [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p001]. The Compute & Networking segment generated $47.4 billion in revenue, representing approximately 78% of total revenue ($60.9 billion) [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p036]. In Q3 FY 2024 alone, Data Center revenue reached a record $14.51 billion, up 279% from a year earlier [0001045810-23-000225:ex-99-press-release-p001].

**Fiscal Year 2025 (ended January 26, 2025):** Revenue growth in fiscal year 2025 was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with demand for the Hopper architecture driving significant growth for the full year [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]. Nvidia began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]. Total revenue more than doubled to $130.5 billion [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-01-26].

**Fiscal Year 2026 (ended January 25, 2026):** Revenue growth in fiscal year 2026 was again driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell architectures representing the majority of Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001]. Total revenue reached $215.9 billion [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25]. In Q3 FY 2026, Data Center revenue was a record $51.2 billion, up 66% from a year earlier [0001045810-25-000228:ex-99-press-release-p001]. The increase in U.S.-based revenue across fiscal years 2026 and 2025 was primarily due to higher U.S.-based Compute & Networking segment demand [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p036].

In summary, data center demand surged in FY 2024, and data center compute and networking platforms were explicitly identified as the driver of revenue growth in both FY 2025 and FY 2026, fueled by successive architecture transitions from Hopper to Blackwell and the broader industry shift toward accelerated computing and generative AI [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p001] [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001] [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001].
